name: Zhao Xiangti
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Yingde Gases Group (no confirmed current role found)
profile: Zhao Xiangti (赵项题) is a founding shareholder of Yingde Gases, once China's largest independent on-site industrial gas supplier (steel-mill oxygen/nitrogen plants), where he previously oversaw finances and later became chairman. He left the chair in 2017 after a shareholder vote; Yingde was then taken private by PAG. Current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Yingde Gases, which he co-founded around 2001 with Sun Zhongguo and Trevor Strutt, grew into China's leading independent industrial-gas supplier to steelmakers and listed in Hong Kong.
notes: Low public profile; English coverage is mostly about the 2016-17 Yingde boardroom dispute (avoid in outreach). MarketScreener lists a Xiang Ti Zhao who led Torch's investment in Yingde, but it is unclear if that is the same person. Yingde is now private (PAG-owned), so no IR route to him.

name: Mustak Hossain
current_role: Chairman, Pataka Group (MD, Pataka Industries Pvt Ltd), Kolkata
profile: Mustak Hossain leads Kolkata-based Pataka Group, founded in 1952 by Giasuddin Biswas as a single biri factory in Murshidabad. Joining in 1980, he diversified it into tobacco, packaged tea and biscuits, textiles (East End Silks), healthcare and real estate (Pataka Infracorp).
interesting_fact: By 1998 Pataka had become India's largest biri maker and marketer, selling over 100 million sticks a day; it entered packaged tea with Pataka Tea in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: The group's philanthropic arm, GD Charitable Society (set up 1989), named after founder Giasuddin Biswas, went on to establish the GD Hospitals and Diabetes Institute in Kolkata in 2007.
notes: Country field blank in input; he is India-based (Kolkata). Low media profile; route via group head office (Pataka House, Mirza Ghalib St, Kolkata) or the contact page.

name: Sudhir Dhingra
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Orient Craft Ltd (Gurugram)
profile: Sudhir Dhingra founded Orient Craft, one of India's largest garment exporters, supplying global fashion brands from factories around Gurugram. A law graduate from a Punjab cotton-farming family, he started exporting shirts in the 1970s and registered Orient Craft in 1978. The company has since rebuilt, declared itself debt-free and is expanding to Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: He told Outlook Business he wanted Orient Craft to be 'a 32-legged animal' that never depends on a single client; by 2014 it had revenue over Rs 1,151 crore and 30,000+ employees.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Fazilka near the Pakistan border, he studied law like his father and grandfather; after a 1972 US trip a London trader friend asked him for 1,000 'cheese cloth' shirts, made in Delhi at Rs 15 each - the Rs 15,000 he calls his 'seed capital'.
notes: Company site orientcraft.com was unreachable when checked; recent press releases (Newsvoir, May 2024+) cover the debt-free turnaround and Jharkhand/Ranchi expansion - a positive hook. Avoid the NPA/debt history.
